findings.message: Anchor the placeholder alternative at the beginning of the input. Its missing ^ allows provider IDs that do not start with aws:/// to pass validation.
findings.evidence: The second regex alternative starts with aws rather than ^aws. Consequently, xaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-abc matches and returns no error; slicing at id[7:] then produces Name "us-east-1a". The previous regex anchored both alternatives and rejected this input.

findings.message: Preserve the entire placeholder name after the zone separator. Selecting only splitted[1] truncates placeholder names containing subsequent slashes, violating the stated contract.
findings.evidence: For aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-group/slot, validation succeeds, but strings.Split followed by splitted[1] returns "i-placeholder-group" instead of "i-placeholder-group/slot". The previous placeholder capture (%s.*) retained the full name. The resulting reference is passed to GetAsgForInstance and InstanceStatus; their implementations are unavailable, so further consequences are unverified.

result.coverage: Inspected TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, the complete staged production file, and all local AwsRefFromProviderId callers. Compared both regex alternatives and extraction behavior.
